title: QCon AI New York 2026 Program Committee Picks: Agent Identity, Context Costs, and Open-Source Infere
gist: QCon AI New York 2026 program committee picks highlight agent identity/authorization (1Password), token compression and caching for context costs, coding agents reshaping engineering orgs, open-source agentic inference with vLLM, agent standards (MCP, A2A, OAuth), and LLM audio. Mostly promotional, but signals where practitioners see production-agent bottlenecks.

insights.claim: Wes Reisz argues traditional identity and authorization models break down as agents take on autonomous work, and that delegated authority, credential management and securing agent interactions must be solved to adopt agentic delivery.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: Agent identity is a gating capability and a market opening for identity vendors.
insights.quote: As agents take on more autonomous work, traditional identity and authorization models start to break down.

insights.claim: A key open problem is delegating authority across subagent chains and giving agents credentials without exposing secrets in their context.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: Secrets management for agents is an emerging product category.
insights.quote: how agents can access the credentials they need without exposing secrets in their context

insights.claim: Standards such as MCP, A2A and OAuth are positioned as the basis for interoperable agent identity, delegated authorization and trust boundaries, organized around which agent is acting, on whose behalf, and how it reaches tools.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: Agent standards are consolidating around MCP/A2A/OAuth; much is still unshipped.

insights.claim: Wes Reisz predicts token compression will become a must-have capability in modern agentic systems because token costs and latency are real constraints for production agents.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: Context compression and caching tooling should see rising demand.
insights.quote: particularly token compression, which I believe will become a must-have capability in modern agentic systems

insights.claim: Learned prompt compression, prefix-cache-aware context alignment and compress-cache-retrieve pipelines are emerging techniques, but they have failure modes affecting tool calling and agent trajectories.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: Cost optimizations can degrade agent reliability; a tradeoff to watch.

insights.claim: For agentic workloads, repeated inference and context growth mean cost per completed task matters more than token price alone.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: Token-price comparisons understate agent costs; efficiency per task is the right metric.
insights.quote: why cost per completed task matters more than token price alone

insights.claim: Engineering structures are changing around coding agents, including team size, rituals, hiring and assessment, leadership, and the future of junior developers, based on conversations with leaders at Anthropic, OpenAI, Shopify and Coinbase.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: Coding agents may compress team sizes and threaten junior developer pipelines.

insights.claim: LLMs are reshaping speech and audio modeling, raising questions about unified multilingual representations, end-to-end versus cascaded architectures, and latency-quality trade-offs for real-time conversational AI.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: Real-time voice AI architecture is still unsettled.
